topic: The Dance of Possibilities: Understanding Quantum Superposition
target_audience: High school students and undergraduate beginners with basic algebra knowledge

sections.title: The Classical Binary World (Prerequisite)
lecture_lines: Our classical world is built on definite binary states.
A switch is either "Off" or "On".
Leaving the room doesn't change its physical position.
animations: Draw a bold text 'DEFINITE' (#FFFFFF) and surround it with a white rectangle.
Create a vertical line with two notches labeled 'On' (top) and 'Off' (bottom) in #888888.
Animate a small square (#FFFFFF) jumping from 'Off' to 'On' without passing through the middle.
A small person silhouette (#FFFFFF) moves to the right edge and fades out; the square stays at 'On'.
Draw two separate square outlines (#FFFFFF); a solid circle (#FFFFFF) appears in the left one.

sections.title: The Quantum Identity Crisis
lecture_lines: In the quantum world, objects act very differently.
Meet Pixel, a cat in a blurry cloud of possibilities.
She exists on the left and right sides simultaneously.
This dynamic state is called a quantum superposition.
Pixel represents multiple potential outcomes existing at once.
animations: Draw a platform (#AAAAAA) with 'Left' and 'Right' labels. Place a cat icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cat.png] (#FFFFFF) in the center.
The cat icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cat.png] fades into a semi-transparent blue cloud (#00FFFF) that expands to cover both sides.
The labels 'Left' and 'Right' both change color to #00FFFF simultaneously.
The blue cloud (#00FFFF) pulses (scales up and down slightly) to show it is a dynamic state.
Text 'State of Superposition' appears in #FFFFFF below the platform.

sections.title: Visualizing the State Vector
lecture_lines: We visualize these states using a geometric state vector.
This arrow points up to represent the "Zero" state.
It rotates right to represent the "One" state.
Diagonally, the arrow represents a mix of both states.
Its direction shows the weight of each classical possibility.
animations: Draw a white circle (#FFFFFF) with a vertical line (up) and a horizontal line (right).
Draw a vector arrow from the center to the top edge (label '|0⟩') in #FFFFFF.
Rotate the vector arrow to point to the right edge (label '|1⟩') in #FFFFFF.
Rotate the vector arrow to a 45-degree angle and change its color to #FFD700.
Label the diagonal vector '|ψ⟩' in #FFD700 to indicate the superposition state.

sections.title: The Math of Probability (Amplitude)
lecture_lines: We use specific values to calculate these outcome weights.
Squaring these values reveals the probability of each state.
As values shift, the likelihood of each outcome changes.
The sum of all probabilities must always equal one.
This ensures a 100 percent total probability for any result.
animations: Display the equation '|ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩' in #FFFFFF using, highlighting α in #FF00FF and β in #00FF00.
Render two bar graphs labeled 'α²' (#FF00FF) and 'β²' (#00FF00) within the that grow to heights 0.6 and 0.4 respectively.
Write 'α² + β² = 1' in #FFFF00 and make the number '1' pulse in size, accompanied by the.

sections.title: The Collapse: The Act of Measurement
lecture_lines: Measuring a system forces its superposition to vanish.
An observer looking causes the state to collapse.
The system instantly snaps into one definite classical state.
animations: Show a spinning coin [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coin.svg] represented by a rotating gray ellipse (#888888).
An eye icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/eye.svg] (#FFFFFF) appears above the coin to represent the act of measurement.
The spinning stops instantly, and the coin [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coin.svg] snaps to a flat circle labeled 'Heads' in #00FF00.

sections.title: Why It Matters: Quantum Computing
lecture_lines: Qubits explore many paths at the exact same time.
A quantum mouse searches every maze route simultaneously.
This massive parallelism solves complex problems in one go.
animations: Show a maze outline (#FFFFFF) with a red dot trying paths one-by-one and hitting dead ends.
Multiple semi-transparent blue dots (#00FFFF) enter the maze and explore every path simultaneously.
One blue dot hits the exit star (#FFFF00), and all other ghostly paths immediately fade away.
